note: Triennial election of the county council, 1911: polled Wednesday 31 May 1911 in six divisions; the other fifteen were returned unopposed. Two seats; "fought on political lines". Johnston and Collen, the old members, had the support of the local Unionist organisations; Acheson, "a Liberal, who came forward as an independent candidate" (Irish News, 1 June 1911, p. 8; "a Radical" in the Belfast News-Letter). 2,261 voters on the register; the poll closed at 8 p.m. and Wm. Wilson, deputy returning officer, announced the result an hour later. W. M. Clow, Robert Chapman and W. J. Johnston withdrew.
